financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone, holding-company-only) basis. Genuinely zero revenue/cost_of_sales/gross_profit/operating_profit -- the Company's only income this quarter was 'Other Income & Gains' of Rs.8,848k (mainly a fair-value gain on FVTPL investment) against Rs.1,520k admin expenses. Main asset is Investment in Subsidiaries (Rs.5,967,233k, unchanged) -- the actual hotel operations and their assets/liabilities sit in the GROUP row. See GROUP row's notes for shared verification/EPS detail.

Jetwing Symphony PLC is a holding company; the standalone COMPANY entity has no revenue of its own (its only income is dividends/other gains from its subsidiaries, held via 'Investment in Subsidiaries' Rs.5,967,233k) -- the actual hoteliering operations sit in the GROUP figures. finance_costs (GROUP) = 'Finance Expenses' (111,766) + 'Exchange (Gain)/Loss from Conversion of Foreign Currency Loan' (13,719 loss) = 125,485, since the schema has no separate FX line and this loss is directly tied to a foreign-currency borrowing. minority_interest = NCI's share of the period's profit/(loss) (-5,437), not a balance-sheet NCI balance. No segmental note is presented in this filing ('There are no distinguishable components to be identified as segments for the Company' -- and no separate Group segmental note is given either). EPS cross-check: GROUP (46,731)/602,188,559 shares = -0.0776 ~= disclosed -0.08; COMPANY 5,129/602,188,559 = 0.0085 ties exactly. No column-swap issues found. Two of the three months in this quarter are the off-season for Sri Lankan tourism per the filing's own note (281,388 tourist arrivals during the quarter) -- relevant context for the quarter's weak/negative profitability, not necessarily company-specific deterioration.

interim_updates.note_text: Jetwing Symphony PLC's Group revenue rose 8% YoY to Rs.828.5mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026; both this quarter and the comparative are off-season for Sri Lankan tourism, per the filing's own disclosure of 281,388 tourist arrivals during the period). Despite the revenue growth, Profit from Operations fell 10% to Rs.186.8mn from Rs.206.5mn, as Administrative Expenses grew 14% (Rs.399.6mn to Rs.457.0mn) -- faster than revenue -- while Marketing & Promotional Expenses fell 14%. Below the operating line, the Exchange Loss on Conversion of a Foreign Currency Loan more than doubled (Rs.6.6mn to Rs.13.7mn loss), and Depreciation & Amortisation rose 11% (Rs.88.6mn to Rs.98.1mn); Finance Expenses were roughly flat (Rs.113.9mn to Rs.111.8mn). Together these pushed the Group from a Rs.2.1mn pre-tax loss a year earlier to a Rs.34.2mn pre-tax loss this quarter -- the filing's own variance column flags this as a -1543% unfavourable swing. The tax charge stayed roughly flat (Rs.18.4mn to Rs.18.0mn) despite the widening loss (consistent with the tourism sector's turnover-based/withholding tax elements rather than a straightforward profit-based charge), so the net loss widened from Rs.20.5mn to Rs.52.2mn (-155% per the filing). The standalone Company (the listed holding entity) has no operating revenue of its own and swung to a small Rs.5.1mn profit (from a Rs.1.7mn loss) purely on an Rs.8.8mn fair-value gain on its FVTPL investment portfolio -- unrelated to the Group's hotel operations. The Company paid its FY2025/26 final dividend of Rs.0.50/share (Rs.301.1mn) on 7 July 2026, reflected as a Dividend Payable at quarter-end.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for JETS -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. No segmental note is presented in this filing at either Group or Company level, so drivers above are limited to P&L line items rather than property/subsidiary-level attribution. eps_basic pct_change for the prior-period comparison is not shown (both periods are losses, so a percentage change is not meaningful) -- direction shown as 'deteriorated' since the loss widened.
interim_updates.takeaway: The wider loss this quarter is a genuine operating deterioration (admin costs outgrew an 8% revenue gain, and operating profit fell 10%), compounded by a larger foreign-currency loan exchange loss -- not an accounting or one-off artefact. However, Q1 (Apr-Jun) is structurally the low season for Sri Lankan tourism, so both this quarter's and last year's losses should be read as seasonal-trough figures, not representative of the full-year run rate; the more important signal is that the YoY comparison of two equivalent off-season quarters still shows genuine deterioration.
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs.828.5mn, +8% YoY, but Profit from Operations fell 10% to Rs.186.8mn as Administrative Expenses grew 14% (outpacing revenue growth)
Exchange Loss on Foreign Currency Loan conversion more than doubled to Rs.13.7mn (from Rs.6.6mn); Finance Expenses roughly flat at Rs.111.8mn
Group swung from a Rs.2.1mn pre-tax loss to a Rs.34.2mn pre-tax loss; net loss widened from Rs.20.5mn to Rs.52.2mn (-155% per the filing's own variance disclosure)
Standalone Company (holding entity, no hotel operations of its own) posted a Rs.5.1mn profit purely from an Rs.8.8mn FVTPL fair-value gain -- unrelated to Group hotel performance
Quarter falls within Sri Lanka's tourism off-season (281,388 tourist arrivals during the period, per the filing's own note)
FY2025/26 final dividend of Rs.0.50/share (Rs.301.1mn total) paid 7 July 2026; shown as Dividend Payable at 30 June 2026
key_drivers: Administrative Expenses (+14% YoY, Rs.399.6mn to Rs.457.0mn) grew faster than the +8% revenue gain, the primary driver of the 10% operating-profit decline -- no segmental breakdown is disclosed to attribute this to a specific property/subsidiary
Exchange Loss on Conversion of Foreign Currency Loan more than doubled YoY (Rs.6.6mn to Rs.13.7mn), directly widening the pre-tax loss beyond the operating decline alone
Depreciation & Amortisation +11% YoY (Rs.88.6mn to Rs.98.1mn), a further drag between operating profit and PBT
